svg.title: One trace across four hops, carried in _meta rather than an HTTP header
svg.desc: A waterfall of four nested spans, all labelled with the one trace identifier 0af7651916cd43dd8448eb211c80319c. The widest bar is the host, covering the whole conversation turn. Inside it, starting later and ending earlier, is the client's bar for a tools/call of get_weather. Inside that is the MCP server's bar for your tool body, and inside that a short bar for the backend SELECT the tool makes. Each bar carries a different span identifier. To the right, a card shows the request that carried the trace: a _meta object holding the two required protocol keys for the protocol version and the client capabilities, and beneath them, shaded, the three tracing keys traceparent, tracestate and baggage, annotated as the only three reserved keys with no reverse-domain prefix. Below, the traceparent value is split into four boxes: a version of 00, the thirty-two character trace identifier that is the same on all four bars, the sixteen character parent span identifier that is new at every hop, and a sampled flag of 01, with a note that only the long field is stable. A panel explains that every other reserved _meta key is a reverse-domain name, that these three are the documented exception kept unprefixed to match existing OpenTelemetry conventions, and that a prefixed spelling names nothing. A closing line says all three keys are optional, that a missing traceparent should start a root span rather than drop the request, and that baggage should be kept boring because it propagates everywhere.
svg.text: One trace id, four spans, and not one HTTP header
traceparent, tracestate and baggage ride inside _meta, so a stdio server joins the same trace.
trace id: the same on all four bars
parent span id: new each hop
parts. Only the long one is stable.
Why these three keys carry no prefix
Every other reserved _meta key is a reverse-domain name. These three are the documented exception, kept
unprefixed to match existing OpenTelemetry conventions. io.modelcontextprotocol/traceparent names nothing.
All three are optional. If no traceparent arrives, start a root span rather than dropping the request. And keep baggage boring: it propagates everywhere.
